citeinfo.origin: Kruger National Park Scientific Services GIS Lab
citeinfo.title: roads_all_2016

descript.abstract: This GIS layer for all roads (including tourist roads, management tracks and firebreaks) in the Kruger National Park.
descript.purpose: All the roads within Kruger National Park including tourist roads, management roads, firebreaks and disused roads. The roads in the 2016 version has been refined from the previous 1:50 000 scale to about 1: 5 000 scale using the 2011 aerial imagery.
descript.supplinf: It is our intention to maintain roads in our database which have fallen into disuse. These are important for historical analysis as they formed boundaries to burn-blocks, ranger sections and other regional divisions.

sngdate.caldate: REQUIRED: The year (and optionally month, or month and day) for which the data set corresponds to the ground.

attracc.attraccr: Length: Software generated - i.e. accurate assuming road locations are accurate. Class: Estimated accuracy > 95% Name: Untested

dataqual.complete: Incomplete: Some non-tourist roads are known to be missing. Attributes currently being updated.

horizpa.horizpar: Based on 1: 50,000 scale topographic data belived to have a 20m RMS error.

procstep.procdesc: Source data as supplied by Surveys and Mapping were converted by GIMS from ReGIS format to ARC/INFO coverages, cleaned and built (tolerances unknown). They were also edge-matched and the national datum transformation from Cape to Hartebeesthoek94 datum was applied with an accuracy higher than that of the actual data.

Roads outside the Park were clipped out of the coverage. An old roads layer from GIS Lab was converted to Shapefile and then Coverage format. The national datum conversion was undertaken (0.5m accuracy). The new roads layer (from Surveys & Mapping via GIMS) was considered spatially accurate but incomplete; the old layer was complete with attributes but spatially inaccurate. The two layers were combined using ArcView to yield the current road layer.

altsys.altenc: Explicit elevation coordinate included with horizontal coordinates

attrdomv.udom: Sequential unique whole numbers that are automatically generated.

dataIdInfo.idAbs:
All the roads within Kruger National Park including tourist roads, management roads, firebreaks and disused roads. The roads in the 2016 version has been refined from the previous 1:50 000 scale to about 1: 5 000 scale using the 2011 & 2018 aerial imagery.

Access definitions:

  • Private - roads that are accessable to staff and authorised guests only

  • Public - roads that are accessable to staff and all guests

  • Staff - roads that are accessable to staff only

Surface definitions:

  • Tar - sealed roads that provide a good all weather surface

  • Graded - unsealed roads that are regularly maintained and are suitable for sedan vehicles

  • Gravel - unsealed roads that have only basic surface maintenance done. High clearence vehicles may be needed

  • Two spoor - unsealed roads that are not maintained. High clearence vehicles needed at a minimum, but 4x4 capability may be needed in places.

  • Disused - unsealed roads that are no longer in regular use and may be overgrown and washed away in places.

  • Rehab - roads that have been permanently closed and actively rehabilitated

prcStep.stepDesc: Source data as supplied by Surveys and Mapping were converted by GIMS from ReGIS format to ARC/INFO coverages, cleaned and built (tolerances unknown). They were also edge-matched and the national datum transformation from Cape to Hartebeesthoek94 datum was applied with an accuracy higher than that of the actual data.

Roads outside the Park were clipped out of the coverage. An old roads layer from GIS Lab was converted to Shapefile and then Coverage format. The national datum conversion was undertaken (0.5m accuracy). The new roads layer (from Surveys & Mapping via GIMS) was considered spatially accurate but incomplete; the old layer was complete with attributes but spatially inaccurate. The two layers were combined using ArcView to yield the current road layer.
